correctness.rationale: Each simple residue zero has a unique Hensel lift; on that disk the valuation is the distance-to-root valuation because the complementary polynomial factor is a unit. Pairwise ball intersections have exact cardinality \(p^{k-\max(t,s)}\) precisely when root lifts agree through min(t,s) digits. The finite-depth joint tails yield the Haar PGF by absolutely convergent indicator sums. A grouped double tail sum gives the exact covariance formula. The resulting numerator gives the complete quadratic sign trichotomy. The included checker passed 1228 direct integer tests over eleven configurations including irrational rational roots, finite root distance and coincident lifts. Finite tests do not establish the theorem.

originality.rationale: Snyder 2023 characterizes valuation trees of products and separately split factors, but does not provide a bivariate joint valuation law or a universal sign trichotomy; his all-rational-linear-factor result does not cover rationally irreducible quadratic examples. Boultinghouse et al. 2023 and Medina–Moll–Rowland 2015 treat single-polynomial valuations. Searches and implication comparisons found no equivalent prior result. The geometric root-ball lemma is classical, not represented as new. Unindexed local zeta and resultant-correlations literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: A logically equivalent root-pair mixed moment formula could be implicit in local zeta-function, resultant, or p-adic tree literature beyond inspected sources.

Published individual polynomial trees can be combined to compute overlap statistics in special cases; the value claim is the explicit all-depth bivariate law and complete quadratic sign frontier, not novelty of ball counting or Hensel lifting.

value.rationale: Individual valuation trees describe marginals, but dependence of valuations of two different integer polynomials at the same input is a distinct natural invariant. The formula is uniform in prime, all depths, arbitrary simple-root polynomials, and includes rationally irreducible quadratics. It yields a complete and sharp positive/negative/zero covariance trichotomy at odd primes, showing an arithmetic phase transition at p=3. This gives a structural root-collision interpretation rather than a table recomputation or arbitrary slice.
